C:/Users/faiz/.local/share/opencode/tool-output/tool_c05b702e1001hLkozCqrtaotQn:  "markdown": "# Icon design trends 2026: From soft 3D to hyper-minimal\n\nDiscover the 8 leading icon design trends for 2026.\n\n[Grace Fussell](https://elements.envato.com/learn/author/gracefussell)20min read13 Jan 2026\n\n![Icon design trends 2026](https://elements.envato.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/2400x1350_JOB-2465_IconDesignTrends2026_BlogHeader.png)\n\nIcons matter more than ever in design. Small but mighty, these tiny symbols take center stage on apps and dashboards, indicating actions, brand recognition, and much more. Major shifts in UX design and [web design](https://elements.envato.com/learn/c/web-design) have arguably made icons more powerful and versatile than logos, which is why it pays to think small.\n\nIn this 2026 icon design trends report, we examine some of the most significant emerging icon design trends, from plush 3D icons that enhance the tactility of mobile apps to variable icons that introduce interactive animation to digital design. We’ll cover aesthetic directions to explore, real-world examples from leading brands, plus pro tips, including how to generate icons with AI.\n\nIcon design is fundamentally about bringing the most aesthetic impact and usability to a graphic within a super small space. They’re often one of the most underrated design tools in a brand’s arsenal, but don’t be fooled by their small stature. They really do pack a punch.\n\n### Full suite of AI. Unlimited creative assets.\n\n[View all](https://elements.envato.com/)\n\n### Mobile App Icon Mockup\n\npitstud\\_design\n\n![Mobile App Icon Mockup](https://elements-resized.envatousercontent.com/elements-cover-images/70322079-49b5-47bf-a912-b0a153cdcbd6?w=900&cf_fit=scale-down&q=85&format=auto&s=06d420e00e504aa95c074c7f37d7d7a996c21a28d2db0db9876cf9af1a7e6e86)\n\n### High Quality iPhone 17 Pro Mockup\n\nrielismee\n\n![High Quality iPhone 17 Pro Mockup](https://elements-resized.envatousercontent.com/elements-cover-images/803359a8-de84-4a95-a437-9f7727616a49?w=900&cf_fit=scale-down&q=85&format=auto&s=bfbaca3884b28862048f8d60bd019bb8c19019f8ca81adec352033955ea4067e)\n\n### iPhone Mockup – High Resolution Scene\n\ncreatifmodeling\n\n![iPhone Mockup – High Resolution Scene](https://elements-resized.envatousercontent.com/elements-cover-images/f52e40a6-3dba-4800-b605-9c1f7b4cbbc3?w=900&cf_fit=scale-down&q=85&format=auto&s=dbd99c131f1f23586e3daa6f988164c125177ead5629f2c12563ab7bb67243d4)\n\n[<](https://elements.envato.com/learn/icon-design-trends#) [>](https://elements.envato.com/learn/icon-design-trends#)\n\n## From trash cans to Duolingo: How icon design trends have evolved\n\nIcon design has undergone significant evolution since the early days of Apple and Microsoft. We started out with [skeuomorphism](https://elements.envato.com/learn/what-is-skeuomorphism), in which icons were designed to mimic real-world objects and textures. Think trash cans and bookshelf icons, detailed with photorealistic materials that gave computer and mobile users a sense of familiarity.\n\n![windows old icon designs ](https://elements.envato.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/windows-old-icons.jpg)\n\nThe flat design movement put an end to all that tactility. Instead, simplicity and symbolic graphics were the order of the day. Over time, flat design evolved into increasingly minimalist icon styles, stripping away excess (and arguably, character) to create clean, calming digital layouts. The problem? Some flat icons were becoming too analogous, leading to users selecting the wrong icon in error.\n\n![flat icon design 2010s](https://elements.envato.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/flat-icons.jpg)\n\nBy the late 2010s, operating systems started to experiment with more playful icon design. Eye-catching details, quirky illustrations, and bold gradients were introduced to boost differentiation and tempt clicks.\n\nFast-forward to today, and we’re in a truly experimental era of icon design trends. The 3D resurgence in icon design makes unlocking your phone an eye-popping experience, and we’re starting to see more variable icon design bringing animation and wit to icon design trends (a special shout-out to the [Duolingo owl](https://design.duolingo.com/identity/logos#icon), Duo, for commitment to the cause).\n\n![duolingo owl mascot icon evolution](https://elements.envato.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/duolingo-mascot.jpg)[Duolingo](https://www.duolingo.com/)‘s Duo icon adopts different expressive personalities and styles depending on the operating system and the level of user interaction.\n\nMeanwhile, the rapid acceleration of AI tools means that icons can be created at speed, with all the bells and whistles, and tech giants like Meta, Google, and Apple realise how powerful icon design can be for converting clicks and actions. It’s the icon’s world, we just live in it.\n\n![word icon evolution](https://elements.envato.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Word-Evolution.jpg)The Microsoft Word icon has been [recently redesigned](https://microsoft.design/articles/fluid-forms-vibrant-colors/) to give it a more 3D, fluid look, complete with subtle gradient details.\n\nWith icons dominating the design world, the diversity of icon design trends continues to expand, exerting influence over interfaces everywhere. Read on to discover the eight icon design trends we predict will make a serious UX stamp in the year ahead.\n\n![icon trend icon design trends 2026](https://elements.envato.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/icon-design_9.jpg)\n\nUse these prompts in [ImageGen](https://labs.envato.com/apps/image-gen) and [ImageEdit](https://labs.envato.com/image-edit) to create the results above. For the icon on the left try this prompt in ImageGen:\n\n> A liquid glass effect 3D icon rendered in a palette of pastel pink, purple and blue, maintaining the simple white logo design in the centre.\n\nFor the alien-inspired design, experiment with this prompt in ImageEdit, using the first image as a starting point:\n\n> Change the pastel colors to a black background and the central logo design to a cute smiling alien logo, with the alien rendered in lime green. Make the corners of the icon more square.\n\n## Icon design trends to watch in 2026\n\nBefore we dive into the icon design trends, we need to ask: What are icon design trends?\n\nIcon design trends tend to follow overarching patterns, with a balance struck between looking like the icon ‘fits in’ within an OS icon set and the need to stand-out and attract attention. This can give all icons designed within a certain time period a particular look and feel, based on textures, line weights, illustration styles, and color palette. While we’re riding the wave of 3D design more generally, however, there’s plenty of space for experimentation, and we’re seeing some really creative icon designs being developed by brands.\n\n### Full suite of AI. Variable icons\n\n**Variable icons** represent the next step in icon design trends, responding to nuanced contexts such as nighttime settings or human interaction. They change form depending on the context, such as light mode and dark mode versions of the same icon, or a subtle animation in response to hover or other interactions. Even an attempted app deletion could be an opportunity to win someone back with an interactive variable icon.\n\n**Variable icons** are more common on OS design systems and advanced dashboards, but it’s possible for any brand to use them with considered development. They’re essential for complex UI flows and adaptive UI, in which they often play a fundamental role in progressing the user journey.\n\n#### Where to use this icon trend?\n\nIf you have a contained system within which to employ variable icons, such as an OS system or website, it’s easier to specify and control how these adaptive icons should behave. AI will be able to assist in developing icons that auto-generate variations. Generally, **Variable icons** are a great way to show that your brand is futuristic and tech-leading, making them a natural fit for digital agencies, tech start-ups, or engineering businesses.\n\n![apple liquid glass icons ](https://elements.envato.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/liquid-glass.jpg)A variety of adaptable Liquid Glass icon options created by [Apple](http://apple.com/).\n\n### Full suite of AI. Here are some ways to integrate the icon design trends into designs for branding, UI, and more.\n\n### Brand design\n\nIcons have become a staple part of a strong brand identity. Often the first touchpoint between a brand and consumer (more so now than a logo design), icons can be given a branded look by selecting a style that aligns with your brand tone. Premium brand? Try the **Multi-materials icons** trend. Playful? **Mascot icons** could be a great choice. As for tech brands, **Variable icons** or **Hyper-minimal line icons** will give your branded apps and websites a futuristic look.\n\n![branded textures icon trend icon design trends 2026](https://elements.envato.com/learn/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/icon-design_10.jpg)\n\nThese 3D icon designs were created using first [ImageGen](https://labs.envato.com/apps/image-gen), before editing the design in [ImageEdit](https://labs.envato.com/image-edit). In this context, carefully crafted icon design achieves more stature within brand identities, so it’s paramount that both designers and businesses give icon design its due attention in 2026.\n\nIcon design now reflects an evolving melting pot of clarity, emotional connection, nostalgia, and intelligent automation. There’s so much to it, blending elements of graphic design, [AI design](https://labs.envato.com/), brand design, motion design, and UI, to create icons that make the user journey truly pleasurable. We hope these icon design trends will fuel your digital ideas in the months to come! And for more brand design inspiration, look no further than our annual [graphic design trend report](https://elements.envato.com/learn/graphic-design-trends), as well as the latest [video and motion design trends](https://elements.envato.com/learn/video-motion-design-trends) set to bring cinematic storytelling back to the heart of content creation in 2026.\n\n## FAQs: Icon design trends 2026\n\n### What icon styles are trending in 2026?\n\nIcon design trends for 2026 are becoming bolder and more expressive, with **Variable icons** contributing dynamic interactivity to interfaces, and **Mascot icons** bringing a cute and fun feel to icon design for the year ahead. We can also see nostalgic styles, such as Retrofuturist icons, becoming more popular, as well as Multi-material icons, which incorporate more 3D tactility through texture.\n\n### How do I choose the right icon style for my project?\n\nNot every icon trend will be suitable for every project. If your project is for a more formal purpose, such as banking or legal services, Multi-material icons will give icon styles a subtle refresh for 2026. Icons aimed at younger audiences can try playful Mascot icons or Soft 3D icons, while tech projects can use Variable icons to add a futuristic edge to their digital projects.\n\n### How can AI help create icons?\n\nAI is useful for promoting consistency across an icon set by preserving styles or details while editing key elements, such as the icon design itself. AI also helps reduce the time it takes to create ideations and iterations of icon designs, allowing you to exercise your creativity more fully within a shorter timeframe. Try using GraphicsGen to create icon graphics, then apply a range of AI styles in **[ImageEdit](https://labs.envato.com/image-edit)**.\n\n### What makes an icon set feel cohesive?\n\nUniform texture, color palette, or edging can contribute to a consistent impression across an icon set. Try to preserve stylistic details across a set, such as a glass texture, pastel palette, or rounded edges.\n\n### Should icons be flat or 3D in 2026?\n\nWhile we are seeing some flat design in icon design in 2026, such as Hyper-minimal line icons, most icon design trends are leaning towards 3D styles, featuring popping highlights, tactile textures, and drop shadowing.\n\n### What file formats are best for exporting icons?\n\nChoose an SVG format for websites and apps, which preserves sharp, scalable detail, or use PNG for general web use when transparency is required. The content I share with you here is timely now, but will be “in the past” pretty fast.\n\nThe Visme content team and I will do our best to update the list regularly with the newest AI design trends and the [design tools](https://visme.co/blog/ai-graphic-design-tools/) to help you achieve them.\n\n### AI Agents - Several AI Tools Working Together\n\nThe most powerful AI design trend for 2026 is the integration of multiple AI tools working in tandem. Each designer using this system has their own favorite combination and some have even created AI Agents for their peers to use.\n\nTheir reasoning behind this lies in the fact that one AI might excel at generating faces but struggle with hands. Or go further and create your own Creative AI agent!\n\n### Using AI for Ideation\n\nUsing AI for ideation is like having an infinitely patient brainstorming partner who can:\n\n- Suggest angles you hadn’t considered\n- Reference styles you might not know about and\n- Help you articulate vague ideas into concrete briefs.\n\nOne thing that all designers and professionals I spoke with agree on is that AI is best at the ideation stage and not for final products. Everything I read, all the videos I watched and all the podcasts I listened to came to the same conclusion.\n\nEveryone agrees AI will help you come up with ideas and even generate first drafts, but it will always need a human touch to reach completion.\n\nAccording to Figma’s 2025 AI Report, [45% of product companies](https://www.figma.com/reports/ai-2025/) are investing in AI for initial concept exploration.\n\nVisme4) Figmas 2025 AI Report\n\n**2024**\n\n**2025**\n\nMore product companies are investing in AI research and development (R&D)\n\nSource: https://www.figma.com/reports/ai-2025/\n\n31%\n\n45%\n\n1/1\n\n![](https://screenshots.visme.co/ed/fe/a2/3f/a82259f1af9a14e7308d07586d9ae67e/slides/sl20_kPBWN4jbS.jpg?v=135)\n\n1 Title\n\nAll Slides\n\nShare\n\nVisme4) Figmas 2025 AI Report\n\nMade with [Visme Presentation Maker](https://www.visme.co/presentation-software?utm_source=CTA&utm_medium=Embed)\n\nThe [State of AI in Design](https://www.stateofaidesign.com/) from Foundation Capital reveals that 72% of designers say that AI enhances ideation for their design work.\n\n![Ai design trends - Figma Stat](https://visme.co/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/AI-design-trend-insight-.png)\n\n[Source](https://www.figma.com/deck/F6P0qVl52W3ngNqyNQCGrl/State-of-AI-in-Design-Report-2025?node-id=1-4173&t=B18KenE36ne7gaxg-1)\n\nFor AI ideation to do its best work, you need to follow a clear structure like this one:\n\n- **Context dump:** Provide all relevant information about the project, audience, and constraints\n- **Divergent exploration:** Ask AI to generate 20-50 wildly different directions\n- **Critical filtering:** Evaluate suggestions through your expertise and taste\n- **Convergent refinement**: Take the best 2-3 concepts and develop them further\n- **Human touch:** Execute the final design manually or with AI assistance\n\nThe context dump and divergent exploration will need a well-formatted prompt. Because the better your prompts, the better your results!\n\nHere’s a prompt draft you can start with:\n\nI'm designing \\[project type\\] for \\[target audience\\]. The goal is \\[objective\\]. The brand is \\[personality/tone\\].\n\nPlease suggest:\n\n- 10 creative concepts that could work for this brief\n- 5 unexpected visual metaphors I might not have considered\n- 3 design styles that would resonate with this audience\n- Potential pitfalls or clichés I should avoid\n\nFor each suggestion, explain why it might work and what makes it different.\n\n### AI-Powered Video Creation\n\nAI video generation is one of the fastest-moving trends and is only making itself more valuable for content creators, designers and marketers.\n\nThat’s why it didn’t take long for Generative AI to progress from image generation to video generation.\n\nThe first videos were super short and often ridiculous. But they’re mostly template-based, so the final output tends to be generic, overly detailed, or already in use by another brand.\n\nWhat AI design generators can do for branding now is more elaborate. Using ChatGPT, Midjourney, Lovable or a combination of several, you can generate more unique logos.\n\nTraditional branding is expensive. A professional brand identity package can cost anywhere from $ 5,000 to $50,000 and take several weeks to complete. AI tools can deliver a complete, customized identity in much less time for a fraction of the cost.\n\nBut there’s a downside. Although AI can generate logos and brand assets, it still requires significant human input.\n\n[Jacob Cass](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jacobcass/), a well-known branding professional, is one of the designers who embraced AI in their processes.\n\nIn a conversation with Mike on the [Mike:ON Podcast](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QwXCJDr7Z6g), Jacob shared:\n\n> _\"Logo design is one of my true passions... The AI presentation design is good for putting the slides together all at once - and then I go in with a fine-tooth comb and make adjustments as needed. Overall, it's a pretty good timesaver.”_\n\n![AI design trends - AI presentation design in Visme](https://visme.co/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/10-2.jpg)\n\n[Source](https://www.reddit.com/r/Entrepreneurs/comments/1npafo8/comment/nh1jo1j/)\n\n### AI for App and Web Designs / Vibe Coding\n\nDesigning apps and websites with AI is another fast-growing trend. It’s so popular that it has its own name: Vibe Coding coined by AI researcher Andrej Karpathy in early 2025.\n\nVibe coding describes a development approach where designers and developers guide AI through natural language prompts to create functional applications, without manually writing code.\n\n![AI design trends - Karpathy Twitter](https://visme.co/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/11-1.jpg)\n\n[Source](https://x.com/karpathy/status/1886192184808149383)\n\nThe concept is simple: you describe what you want your app to do, and the AI generates the code in real-time, rendering it on screen. The process feels less like programming and more like having a conversation with a creative partner who understands both design and development.\n\nEven though vibe coding is quickly reshaping software development by making it faster, more accessible and collaborative, the issue is that it’s not perfect and can break at any time. If you don’t know how to code well, you won’t know how to fix it.\n\n[Amar Ratnakar Naik](https://www.linkedin.com/in/amarnaik/), an AI leader at Telus, shares succinctly in a [LinkedIn article](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/stop-vibecoding-start-engineering-2026-trend-you-cant-naik-ox7de/),\n\n“The future doesn’t belong to those who can just prompt an LLM, it belongs to those who can fix what the LLM broke.”\n\nHe continues with his thoughts on a major myth: AI will replace engineers.\n\n> _“No,” he remarks, “AI will replace the engineers who never learned how things actually work. Meanwhile, those who understand protocols, patterns, observability, and scaling? They're about to become the most expensive hires in the room.”_\n\nIf you’re ready to try vibecoding, here are some of the most popular tools:\n\n- **Lovable:** Best for full-stack web applications with database integration\n- **Bolt.new:** Excellent for rapid prototyping with frameworks like Next.js\n- **v0 by Vercel:** Ideal for generating React components and UI blocks\n- **Cursor:** Perfect for developers who want AI assistance within their IDE\n- **Replit:** Great for collaborative coding with built-in AI help\n\n### AI Flows for UI\n\nUI/UX Designers are also leveraging AI for their work, saving a significant amount of time in the process. AI flows in UI refer to using AI agents to map out user journeys, from wireframes to high-fidelity prototypes, while maintaining consistency across screens and states.\n\nInstead of manually creating every variation of a button or modal, designers describe the system once and AI generates all the necessary components and states. One of the latest tools that helps with this trend is Figma Make, an AI agent inside Figma.\n\nOne of the biggest voices for learning and improving UI flows is [Zander Whitehurst](https://www.linkedin.com/in/zanderwhitehurst/) from Memorisely. One of their [latest videos](https://www.instagram.com/p/DOLo5QOjNpy/) is a perfect example of how designers can incorporate AI into their flows, without it taking away the human element.\n\n![AI design trends - AI videos Zander Whitehurst from Memorisely](https://visme.co/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/12-1.jpg)\n\n[Source](https://www.instagram.com/p/DOLo5QOjNpy/)\n\n### AI For Social Media Visual Posts and Ads\n\nCreating social media designs used to mean hours in Adobe platforms or customizing with templates one by one. Now the process is easier than ever with AI.\n\nThese tools are changing how marketers, designers and social media managers create scroll-stopping content like videos, graphics and ads.\n\nThe constant pressure to post consistently across multiple platforms lies heavily on creative social teams. This has made AI increasingly practical for their day-to-day work.\n\nAccording to [Hootsuite’s Social Trends Repor](https://hootsuite.widen.net/s/psc5swlkbh/hootsuitesocialtrends2025_report_en) t,\n\n> _“What fueled this growth is the perpetual need for more content. Because today, an always-on social presence is vital for staying competitive and delivering ROI.” In fact, research conducted by Hootsuite and Critical Truth indicates that brands should be aiming to create and post between [48 and 72 posts per week](https://blog.hootsuite.com/how-often-to-post-on-social-media/?utm_campaign=all-tier_1_campaigns-trends_2025-glo-none-------&utm_source=report&utm_medium=owned_content&utm_content=) across platforms._\n\n![Ai design trends -Hootsuite’s Social Trends Report](https://visme.co/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/13-1.jpg)\n\n[Source](https://hootsuite.widen.net/s/psc5swlkbh/hootsuitesocialtrends2025_report_en)\n\nAs I mentioned earlier, it is now more common to use multiple tools instead of a single one.\n\nFor example, here’s a [LinkedIn post](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/shlomogenchin_a-new-ad-i-created-for-my-client-hibob-ugcPost-7378415430694100992-ksTy/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAAK5if4B-A-Hea_fxGT_DDO8b2i9kGsXYec) explaining how social designers are creating ads with the help of AI workflows.\n\nThe video shared in the post was created by [Shlomo Genchin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shlomogenchin/) for one of his clients.\n\nAside from generating numerous social media posts in the same dimensions, AI also assists with reformatting and repurposing for different sizes and purposes. Visme’s social media and community manager, Chelse Hensley shared her thoughts on this during a [podcast with Mike Allton](https://www.agorapulse.com/blog/podcasts/social-pulse-podcast/the-social-media-strategists-secret-turning-ideas-into-scroll-stopping-visuals/) from Agorapulse.\n\n> _\"Even though you're reformatting them, just make sure you put the soul back into it. I've been a social media manager for over 10 years now. I don't want to lose the soul of what it's supposed to be... with the growth of all these AI tools, every post may start to look the same. So even though you're reformatting them, just make sure you put the soul back into it.\"_\n\nJust one more bit of proof that in the end, no matter how much AI can help, it still needs the human touch or soul, to reach final completion.\n\n### AI For Absurdity, Comedy and Shitposting\n\nNot all design is serious business. For individuals with a sense of comedic creativity, AI is one of the most entertaining tools available today. Ideating and creating absurd visuals for the sake of comedy is my favorite trend on this list.\n\nComedy and virality are intimately connected. Now that everyone scrolls past polished ads and content riddled with sameness, absurdist AI content makes people stop, laugh and share. Brands and creators that embrace this chaotic energy connect with audiences on a human level because we all need a laugh.\n\nTake, for example, the crazy mashups with funny names like Tung Tung Tung Sahur, Tralalero Tralala and Ballerina Cappuccina. These AI creations, known as [Italian Brain Rot](https://www.instagram.com/p/DIGpdL3R9TP/), are among the most viral trends powered by AI.\n\n[Fabian Mosele](https://www.linkedin.com/in/fabian-mosele/), an early pioneer of the Brain Rot universe, shared in [a Medium article](https://medium.com/@fabianmosele/italian-brainrot-when-ai-slop-becomes-culture-4cff8c344d66),\n\n> _\"At first, it was all just a joke. We were pretending and laughing at the absurdity of characters like Trallallero Trallallà and Tung Tung Tung Sahur. These creations were never meant to fit into a conventional cartoon. Italian Brainrot couldn't have existed in a non-AI This is one where he combined SMEG appliances with Croc Shoes.\n\n![AI design trends - AI Mashups on LinkedIn](https://visme.co/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/15.jpg)\n\n[Source](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/garthmanthe_i-live-for-over-the-top-mash-ups-%F0%9D%97%96%F0%9D%97%BF%F0%9D%97%BC%F0%9D%97%B0%F0%9D%98%80-activity-7378670687923650561-z1jq/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAAK5if4B-A-Hea_fxGT_DDO8b2i9kGsXYec)\n\nOne of the professionals I talked with, Justin Kramm, runs a creative agency that openly promotes the fact that they use AI to create.\n\nA few days after we talked, he published a promotional video for his company, ShitShow Creative.\n\nIt’s a trailer for Planet ShitShow and it’s all made with AI. Here’s one example I made: a lemon drinking coffee on the subway.\n\n![AI image generator - image created with AI image generator](https://visme.co/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/16.jpg)\n\n### Anti-AI: Purposefully Not Using AI at All\n\nFinally, the last trend is precisely the opposite of all the others. Anti-AI, or not using AI at all.\n\nWhat’s the reasoning behind Anti-AI? Aside from the people who are simply against change, the sentiment is based on how AI stole work from designers, illustrators and artists to train the models.\n\nLooking back at how AI image generation started, the developers fed the system with millions of pieces of art, design and general information. They essentially gave AI free access to everything that existed on the Internet.\n\nThe designers and [artists who were affected](https://medium.com/@mkwashbu/generative-artificial-intelligence-and-its-impacts-on-artists-54a2eeafa78e) by this mass event are the first ones to tell you that AI is evil, and that they refuse to use it. The [Reddit subreddit r/antiai](https://www.reddit.com/r/antiai/) has over 300,000 visitors and 20,000 shared posts.\n\nIt’s not just about not using AI directly, but some are tired of seeing mostly AI-generated visuals when doing visual research, looking for references and stock photography.\n\nSites like Pinterest were so overloaded with AI-generated content that they [created an AI label](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/pinterest-labeling-tag-ai-generated-images-pins/741986/) for visitors to distinguish between authentic and AI-slop.\n\nRachel K, a digital marketer and content manager, recently shared [her sentiments](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/rachel-k-95a727193_marketing-socialmediamanagers-activity-7380915300583653396-BILC?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAAK5if4B-A-Hea_fxGT_DDO8b2i9kGsXYec) on the subject on LinkedIn.\n\n![AI design trends - Rachel K thoughs on AI ](https://visme.co/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/17.jpg)\n\n[Source](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ilenia-notarangelo-b2766a39_motiondesign-illustrationsystem-designforchange-activity-7380970361594605568-vQPL?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAAK5if4B-A-Hea_fxGT_DDO8b2i9kGsXYec)\n\nTurns out she’s not the only one.\n\n![AI design trends -IIlenia Notarnagelo thoughs on AI ](https://visme.co/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/18.jpg)\n\nI wanted to gain a clear understanding of people's thoughts, so I conducted a poll on LinkedIn asking, “Where do you stand on the use of AI for creative tasks?” The results were interesting. Anti-AI is prevalent, but what people are really saying is that creatives need to find a balance between human and AI.\n\n![AI design trends - Orana's Polls on AI](https://visme.co/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Oranas-Polls-on-AI.png)\n\n[Source](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oranavelarde_which-one-are-you-activity-7380996849316388865-IKiQ?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAAK5if4B-A-Hea_fxGT_DDO8b2i9kGsXYec)\n\n## Future Predictions: AI Design Trend for 2027\n\nWe can all attest that AI itself is no longer a trend in its own right. AI is here to stay and has taken its place in the designer toolbox.\n\nThe 11 AI Design trends we examined here are only going to continue evolving and shaping graphic design trends.\n\nLooking to the future of AI in design is exciting, as long as you keep one thing in mind. To always add a good dose of human touch to any project created with the help of AI.\n\nBut what about the sentiment that many designers share?\n\n### Will AI Take Over Our Jobs?\n\nThe consensus among industry leaders is clear. AI won't replace designers who adapt, but it will redefine what design means. The future belongs to professionals who can integrate AI tools while bringing irreplaceable human qualities, such as strategic thinking, emotional intelligence, cultural awareness, and authentic creativity, to every project.\n\nTom May, professional design writer, explains,\n\n> _“In an ideal world, AI would be used only for the repetitive, mechanical work of design: things like writing alt text and producing basic website wireframes._\n>\n> _However, I think it's inevitable that it will be increasingly used for the creative and craft side too, which means everything will look and feel the same. This already happened in the 2010s when websites and apps started looking and feeling very similar. And there is a benefit to the consumer because people now instinctively know how to use an app, for instance, without needing a training manual. However, it has robbed design of a lot of its creativity and imagination, and I think AI will push design further in that direction.”_\n\nChris Do, an exceptional branding expert, also has a lot to say about AI and how important it is to learn the skills that will help you always stay on top. Please try again later.\n\nWatch later\n\nShare\n\nCopy link\n\nWatch on\n\n0:00\n\n0:00 / 18:46\n\n•Live\n\n•\n\n### How Will AI Change Design Education?\n\nThe integration of AI into design is reshaping how the next generation learns and practices the craft.\n\nElizabeth Lin, in a conversation on the [Design Better podcast](https://designbetterpodcast.com/p/elizabeth-lin?hide_intro_popup=true), highlights that design schools are now grappling with how to incorporate AI literacy while maintaining core creative principles. The challenge isn't just teaching students to use AI tools; it's preparing them to think strategically about when and how to deploy these technologies.\n\nPlatforms like [Coursiv](https://coursiv.io/en) are filling this educational gap, offering courses specifically focused on AI-assisted design workflows. Meanwhile, content designers are exploring [how their role evolves in an AI-powered world](https://uxdesign.cc/the-future-of-content-design-in-an-ai-world-bb58ba26455c). They’re striving to strike a balance between automation and human creativity.\n\n### Will the Human-AI Balance Stay Relevant?\n\nDespite the ongoing advancement of AI into the design space, the human-AI balance will remain critical.\n\nInterestingly, recent ad campaigns from both [Anthropic and OpenAI](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/amar-chohan_anthropic-and-openai-both-launched-ad-campaigns-ugcPost-7378373249346273280-DPGF?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_ios&rcm=ACoAAAK5if4B-A-Hea_fxGT_DDO8b2i9kGsXYec) emphasize AI as a collaborative tool rather than a replacement for human intelligence. This message resonates with designers who view AI as augmenting rather than replacing their expertise.\n\nAccording to [Superside's analysis,](https://www.superside.com/blog/enterprise-ai-design-trends) enterprise design teams are finding success by establishing clear guidelines on when to use AI and when human judgment is non-negotiable. The most effective teams treat AI as a junior designer: great for exploration and iteration, but requiring senior oversight for final decisions.\n\n![AI design trends -Superside thoughts on AI ](https://visme.co/blog/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/19.jpg)\n\n[Source](https://www.superside.com/blog/enterprise-ai-design-trends)\n\n### Is There an AI Generational Divide?\n\nNow and in the future, there will always be a generational divide in AI adoption. Gen Z designers, who are entering the workforce with AI as a native tool, approach design fundamentally differently than their predecessors.\n\nAs explored in an analysis of [how Gen Z uses AI](https://medium.com/@armankamran/gen-z-ai-how-generative-ai-is-reshaping-the-future-of-an-entire-generation-3ed4f497be79), younger designers don't see AI adoption as optional; it's simply another tool in their kit, like Figma or Adobe Creative Suite. They're more comfortable experimenting, failing fast with AI, and iterating rapidly.\n\nThis generational perspective suggests that debates about whether to use AI will soon feel as dated as arguments against digital design tools in the 1990s. The future of design isn't human vs. AI, it's about designers who can fluently collaborate with both.\n\n## AI Design Trend FAQs\n\n### What are the latest AI trends?\n\nThe latest AI trends for 2025-2026 include:\n\n- Vibe coding for rapid app development\n- AI-powered video creation with looks like Sora 2\n- Character-consistent AI photography\n- Multimodal AI agents that combine multiple tools\n- AI branding systems that generate complete brand identities from text prompts.\n\n### What is Gen Z design style?\n\nGen Z design embraces maximalism, bold experimentation and seamless integration of AI tools in the creative process.\n\nThey favor authentic, imperfect aesthetics over polished perfection. Their creations mix retro and futuristic elements and prioritize accessibility and inclusivity. [Over 70% of Gen Z](https://www.forbes.com/sites/johnkoetsier/2023/09/09/generative-ai-generation-gap-70-of-gen-z-use-it-while-gen-x-boomers-dont-get-it/) use AI weekly for creative work, treating it as just another part of their toolkit.\n\n### Which design is trending now?\n\nThere’s no single design trend currently trending. Design trends typically rise alongside others. So, as of October 2025, some design trends include:\n\n- Inflated, furry or shiny 3D objects\n- Abstract shapes used as backgrounds and support visuals\n- Geometric simplicity\n- Maximum minimalism\n- Pixelized typography\n\n### Does graphic design have a future with AI?\n\nYes, absolutely. AI is dissolving entry-level tasks but elevating the role of experienced designers. According to Figma’s 2025 AI Report, 30% of designers strongly agree that AI significantly enhances their efficiency and that number is steadily increasing.\n\nThe future belongs to designers who use AI as a powerful tool while bringing human creativity, strategic thinking and cultural understanding that AI cannot replicate.\n\n### What will be the biggest graphic design trend in 2026?\n\nThe combination of multiple AI tools in unified workflows (AI Agents) will be the defining trend of 2026. Rather than using one platform, designers will continue to orchestrate several specialized AI tools for ideation, generation and refinement. They’ll continue to create results impossible with any single tool alone.\n\n### Can ChatGPT do graphic design?\n\nYes, ChatGPT can do graphic design but it depends on your prompt. The custom GPT, [Graphic Designer](https://chatgpt.com/g/g-lPeUc0axE-graphic-designer) can create acceptable design renders from your prompts. The GPT asks you lots of questions to generate the best design possible for you.\n\nThat said, a graphic design created with ChatGPT will still need human input to be the best it can be. Only AI is not enough.\n\n## Keep Up with Future Trends Using the Best AI Design Tool\n\nThe future of design isn't about choosing between human creativity and artificial intelligence; it's about mastering the collaboration between both.\n\nAs we have seen, the AI creative design trends shaping 2026 reveal one overarching truth: AI amplifies human potential when used strategically.\n\nSo, whether you're leveraging AI in product design trend developments, exploring AI in modern web design trends or implementing AI website design trends for your clients, the key is finding the right balance.\n\nThe designers who are thriving aren't the ones using the most AI tools or avoiding them entirely. They're the ones who understand when to ideate with AI, when to generate with AI, and when to step in with irreplaceable human judgment, emotional intelligence and creative vision.\n\nReady to explore how AI can amplify your design process while keeping your unique creative voice intact? [​](https://docs.mayar.id/api-reference/webhook/history#param-id)

id

string<uuid>

required

integer (timestamp)

required

nextDelivery

string \| null

required

Timestamp of the next delivery attempt (if any).

paymentLinkId

string<uuid>

required

Associated payment link ID.

payload

string (JSON string)

required

[​](https://docs.mayar.id/api-reference/webhook/history#param-status)

status

string

required

Delivery status (example: `"SUCCESS"`).

[​](https://docs.mayar.id/api-reference/webhook/history#param-type)

type

string

required

[​](https://docs.mayar.id/api-reference/webhook/history#param-updated-at)

updatedAt

integer (timestamp)

required

Last update timestamp.

[​](https://docs.mayar.id/api-reference/webhook/history#param-user-id)

userId

string

required

User ID who owns this webhook.

paymentLinkTransactionId

string<uuid>

required

urlDestination

string (URL)

required

responsePayload

string \| null

required

Response returned from the destination endpoint.

string

required
